messages:
jess_customer: Hey team — customer ACME reports intermittent 600-1200ms p95 on requests. Their Console shows region eu-west-1 but the request traces show requests served from us-east-1. They notice higher latency and billing oddities. Anyone seen dashboard vs served-region mismatch before?

maya_support: Ugh, thanks for flagging. Do we have an example request id or curl+response headers? Also which customer (org id)?

jess_customer: Org: acme-inc, sample req id: r_20260317_01. Here's the curl we ran and the response headers we captured:

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk.acme-org-xxx" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \
  https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
```

Response headers:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-redwood-served-from: us-east-1
x-redwood-served-pop: us-east-1a
x-redwood-routing-reason: fallback_capacity_unavailable
x-request-id: r_20260317_01
x-auth-scope: hosted
content-type: application/json
```

The Console UI shows the session pinned to eu-west-1 and billing page attributes these tokens to EU. Customer says billing shows higher egress costs because traffic actually went to us-east.

rita_eng: That x-redwood-routing-reason header is interesting — fallback_capacity_unavailable implies the eu pool refused due to no available reserved slots and we fell back to global/other-pop. Can you also paste the full audit log line for r_20260317_01?

jess_customer: Pasted below from their trace log (redacted):
```
[2026-03-17T12:01:15Z] INFO route_decision req=r_20260317_01 user=acme-inc pref_region=eu-west-1 token_type=hosted -> candidate_pools=[eu-west-1,dedicated-eu] selected=us-east-1 fallback_reason=capacity_unavailable
```

maya_support: @rita_eng @leo_platform customer says they have no Dedicated for this org, purely hosted. They expect Console to show where the request was actually served (for troubleshooting). Right now Console shows preferred region and billing attribution by org preference which is confusing.

leo_platform: Quick notes from routing side: + If token is hosted (x-auth-scope: hosted) we attempt preferred-region routing first. + If preferred region has no capacity we select fastest available region (which could be us-east). + Console currently displays the "configured/preferred" region and the billing attribution region, but not necessarily the runtime served_pop. That's a product/observability gap.

ops-bot: [12:03:16] deploy: autoscaler-eu-west trimmed pool by -2 GPUs due to ephemeral spike at 12:00:58; fallback events count increased by 18 in last 10m.

rita_eng: Repro steps for engineering to validate: 1) Use a hosted token for an EU-pref org. 2) Send a burst of >100 concurrent short requests with header X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1. 3) Observe routing headers and routing decision logs. We should hit fallback path if autoscaler lags. I'll run a small load test from my workstation now.

jess_customer: Customer wants two things: (1) Console to show "served_pop" alongside configured region and (2) immediate mitigation: if requests are falling back cross-region, can we force routing to fail instead of routing to a remote pop? They prefer errors over cross-region latencies/billing surprises.

leo_platform: For immediate mitigation: we can flip tenant-level flag enforce_region_preference=true which will cause requests to 503 when preferred region has no capacity. That avoids cross-region serving. It's a safe opt-in. I'll open a tenant config ticket and escalate.

maya_support: Please do—customer asked to opt-in. Also we need a UI change request: Console should show served pop with header examples (x-redwood-served-from). I'll file a product ticket with repro and logs.

rita_eng: Follow-up from my quick test: I reproduced fallback. Sample decision log:
```
[2026-03-17T12:04:02Z] route_decision req=test123 pref=eu-west-1 selected=us-east-1 reason=fallback_capacity_unavailable autoscaler_event=scale_down_recent
```
Headers returned include x-redwood-served-from. So server-side is correct. This is purely a UI/telemetry mapping bug where Console maps billing/tenant preference to region badge instead of last_served_pop.

leo_platform: Action items: 1) ops: set enforce_region_preference=true for acme-inc (temporary) — @maya_support to confirm with customer. 2) product: add served_pop column on request traces and on org-level recent requests page. 3) engineering: add a dashboard metric for fallback_rate by region and surface in Console. 4) Billing: run quick audit to reclassify the affected requests if we want to credit cross-region charges for the incident window.

maya_support: I'll confirm opt-in with customer now. Jess — can you let them know that we can flip the flag and that we'll follow up with a product ticket and possible billing credit? :thumbsup:

jess_customer: Confirmed with ACME — they want the region-enforcement flag enabled for the next 24h while they validate. Thanks, team.

rita_eng: I'll attach the routing logs and the tiny load test script to the product ticket so product + UI can reproduce easily.

leo_platform: I'll also drop a short note in the runbook: when Console shows a different region than x-redwood-served-from, check for fallback_capacity_unavailable and consider enforce_region_preference.

maya_support: Closing loop — created internal ticket RED-3421 (opt-in enforcement + UI fix + billing audit). Will update ACME and schedule follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
